body:
In [10.4.16](https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/blob/master/5.0/en/0x19-V10-OAuth2-and-OIDC.md#v104-oauth-authorization-server) we currently have the following:

| # | Description | Level | #v5.0.be |
| :---: | :--- | :---: | :---: |
| **10.4.16** | Verify that the client is confidential and the authorization server requires the use of strong client authentication methods (based on public-key cryptography and resistant to replay attacks), such as mutual TLS (mTLS) or private key JWT ('private_key_jwt'). | 3 | v5.0.be-51.4.10 |


It appears that 'private_key_jwt' refers to a specific mode where as mTLS is a more general mechanism. I find that mix a little confusing, could we either refer to a couple of specific modes or a couple of general mechanism @randomstuff?

comments.body:
~~doh 🤦‍♂️~~

It kind of feels like this point got lost so I would be tempted to close #2897 as it got mostly resolved by #2931 and there is just this point remaining. What do you think @elarlang ?

Colleagues, I have some doubts regarding "confidential" in context of this requirement. 
And to align mentioning of authentication mechanisms, I would like to stick to not go into details here.
Should we put this requirement in following way:

> Verify that the client is **authenticated** and the authorization server requires the use of strong client authentication methods (based on public-key cryptography and resistant to replay attacks), such as mutual TLS (mTLS) or private key JWT.

Regarding capitalization we have discussion in #1875 . 
Potentially it could be be put as "Mutual TLS (mTLS) or Private Key JWT", as it used in OAuth: https://oauth.net/private-key-jwt. But as agreed, we should wait for approach on capitalization and then make change, if needed.
"confidential client" is specific term for OAuth, it is a client type (public client and confidential client), please see the chapter text.

@elarlang thank you for explanation! This point is clear for me now. 
And I noticed that this capitalization topic of m(M)utual TLS (mTLS)) is actual for other requirements in this chapter -- different approach used in requirements description. Will add this to (https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/issues/1875#issuecomment-2787251891) also.
@randomstuff I think you still need to look at this one? Looks like the commit above was a typo and actually refers to something else
Yes, I don't know why this commit ended up here and why *I* appear to have added  it :)

@tghosth, shall we use:

> Verify that the client is confidential and the authorization server requires the use of strong client authentication methods (based on public-key cryptography and resistant to replay attacks), such  mutual TLS ('tls_client_auth', 'self_signed_tls_client_auth') or private key JWT ('private_key_jwt').

> self_signed_tls_client_auth

Is this considered secure? It sounds bad

"self_signed_tls_client_auth" is applicable and can be used for some configurations. According to [RFC 8705](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc8705) the requirement (prerequisite) here is to register this certificate with the Authorization server. And the Authorization server has become like a Certificate authority for this case. So if other conditions are met (proper certificate validation, etc.), it is as secure as using regular certificate authorization by Trusted Third Party.
And I support version suggested @randomstuff  with mentioning exact OAuth authentication parameters, this will help in implementation and testing.

> "self_signed_tls_client_auth" is applicable and can be used for some configurations. According to [RFC 8705](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc8705) the requirement (prerequisite) here is to register this certificate with the Authorization server. 

Ok so basically in the "self_signed_tls_client_auth" mechanism, the client has to use a certificate that was previously registered with the server so whilst it is self-signed, it is specifically registered as the client's certificate so it is not an issue. Thanks for the clarification @oleksiidov, I am going to open a PR and add a note along those lines.
Thanks @randomstuff and @oleksiidov for your help in getting this resolved!

title: Clarify 10.4.16 (v5.0.be-51.4.10)
